newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tugboat workers end long strike at French oil port.
newsitem.headline: Tugboat workers end long strike at French oil port.

text.p: A tugboat strike which had disrupted key oil refining terminals near Marseille, southern France, ended on Friday with a pledge to resume normal operations at 1500 GMT, port officials said.

The strike for better conditions at the twin ports of Fos and Lavera had stretched sporadically over two months but hardened to the point where some oil tankers were prevented from unloading this week.
"We are back to normal at five o'clock (1500 GMT)," a port traffic official said, adding the strike had not however seriously penalised oil refineries in the region.
The area is a major Mediterranean coastal refining centre but suffers overcapacity with four plants operated by BP France, Shell France, Total and Esso France.
Oil tankers depend on tugboats for delicate manoeuvres, especially when loaded, though container ships and other dry bulk vessels can cope without them, a port spokesman said.
The tugboat workers went on a partial strike for better conditions and in protest at plans to cut jobs in early April and toughened their campaign with a total stoppage this week.
